Alex: quick idea: add a tiny 'hotkey shepherd' optimization to reduce repeated rehydrates for ultra-hot prefixes
Maria: what's the key invariant?
Alex: token is cooperative (no heavy fencing). encodes level, epoch, last-write-hash. readers short-circuit if epoch matches
Sam: similar to soft-pin but richer. how avoid stale tombstones?
Kevin: worry about demote+write races. shepherd must be optimization only; canonical path remains leases + tombstone propagation
Alex: agreed. writers bump epoch in coord layer and emit async invalidate hooks. tokens speed reads but are invalidated on conflicting writes
Sam: eviction: prefer shedding non-shepherd slabs; reclaim shepherded slices only after bounded grace. add eviction_credit per token to bound memory impact and preserve fairness
Maria: telemetry: token_hit_rate, invalidation_rate, stale_sample_count, read_latency_quantiles with/without token, token_memory_overhead
Kevin: tests: unit races for epoch bump; multi-node chaos with node crash; staged canary 0.5% traffic with strict stale/read latency gates
ops-bot: scheduled canary: cluster=canary-3 window=2h start=2026-04-02T03:00Z
Alex: I'll draft RFC and reference impl. include token lifecycle diagram and explicit invariants
Maria: migrate plan + KB + dashboards + rollback playbook needed
Sam: I'll own chaos tests
Kevin: will write invariants tomorrow
Alex: posting RFC soon :thumbsup:
